newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia rubber softens, traders ignore INRO.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia rubber softens, traders ignore INRO.

text.p: Indonesian tyre-grade SIR20 offer prices softened in early trading on Friday and traders said they were largely ignoring a plan by the International Natural Rubber Organisation (INRO) to resume market intervention.
Traders said U.S. buyers bought rubber at 46.50 U.S. cents/lb fob Palembang for July/August shipment overnight while European buyers purchased SIR20 at 47.25 also for July/August shipment fob Medan.
"Offer prices in other centres have declined in line with the deals in Palembang and Medan. There is no activity in the market this morning and buying interest is zero," said one trader.
Traders said they were ignoring INRO's plan to resume market intervention to stabilise prices following the launch of a new global accord.

"We used to be happy with such news. But the fact is that Indonesia produces tens of thousands of tonnes of rubber each month. We are always in doubt about how much rubber INRO can buy from us," said another trader.
"We believe that INRO can only purchase at most 100 tonnes. It's so small," he said.
Traders said their attention was on the tight supply in the local market.

"Supply is quite tight in the local market because many rubber collectors are hoarding stocks, looking for better prices. In addition, afternoon rains in some of the rubber centres have affected the tapping activities," said one trader.

Traders said offer prices were quoted at 46.50 for July shipment and at 47.00 for August shipment fob Palembang. Traders offered rubber at 47.25 fob Medan for August shipment, 46.75 fob Padang and 46.50 fob Pontianak and Jambi.
